title: local-first RAG authoring sandbox and validate-playground
author: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Motivation: Provide a lightweight, local-first RAG authoring playground that lets engineers iterate on retrieval strategies and prompt variants without requiring cloud credentials or a remote index. This quickstart is aimed at product/infra engineers who want deterministic, reproducible authoring flows: live indexing, offline similarity search (annoy/nmslib fallback), deterministic prompt evaluation harness, and live validation assertions against a small corpus.

What this PR adds (single continuous description): Adds a new example project under examples/local-authoring-sandbox. The sandbox contains: 1) devcontainer and docker-compose for a reproducible local environment (Redis-based KV shim, local Annoy index builder, a tiny HTTP shim that emulates Redwood streaming responses), 2) an authoring CLI (authorctl) that scaffolds documents, builds indices, runs example prompts and records structured predictions, 3) a validate-playground web app (Svelte) which runs a suite of prompt+retrieval test cases and displays token-level traces and similarity diagnostics, 4) a set of canonical prompt test cases and a baseline evaluation harness that records output diffs for regression detection. The README includes a step-by-step quickstart and troubleshooting notes for common local pitfalls (port collisions, index memory tuning).

Files & code highlights: - examples/local-authoring-sandbox/devcontainer.json and Dockerfiles for a reproducible dev environment. - examples/local-authoring-sandbox/authorctl: small Python CLI (click) that exposes `init`, `index`, `run`, and `record` commands; index command supports ANN (annoy) and brute-force fallback; run supports deterministic RNG and tokenization stubs for reproducible traces. - examples/local-authoring-sandbox/validate-playground: Svelte app that consumes recorded runs and displays: retrieval hit table, prompt transformations, and a playback of generated token traces. - docs/snippets/local-authoring-guides.md: new quickstart doc included in the docs site navigation. - small shim server examples/local-authoring-sandbox/shim_server: a tiny fastapi app that returns mock streaming chunks to validate client-side streaming logic locally.

Checklist (author): - [x] Add example repo skeleton + devcontainer - [x] Implement authorctl index/run/record - [x] Add validate-playground UI + test cases - [x] Add docs quickstart and troubleshooting - [x] Add unit tests for authorctl key codepaths - [x] Add CI job (examples-ci) to smoke the devcontainer build and run basic `authorctl index` command.

Usage summary: - git clone && open in VS Code devcontainer OR docker-compose up - authorctl init --corpus sample_data/ - authorctl index --method annoy --params "n_trees=8" - authorctl run --case example_1 --deterministic true - open validate-playground at http://localhost:3000 to inspect retrieval and traces

Compatibility notes: This example intentionally avoids requiring Redwood API keys. It includes a small adapter to plug into Redwood SDK stubs so teams can switch to real inference with a single config change. The example also demonstrates model variant fallback by simulating two model profiles in the shim server.

Security and privacy: The sandbox stores all data locally. The README warns about copying production PII into the sample corpus and suggests redaction scripts included under examples/local-authoring-sandbox/scripts/redact_sample.sh.

Why different from existing RAG quickstarts: Existing quickstarts focus on cloud-backed indices or fully managed pipelines; this PR emphasizes a local-first iterative loop (authoring + live validation) to shorten the feedback loop for prompt engineering and retrieval ranking experiments.

Migration/rollback: Deleting the examples/local-authoring-sandbox directory reverts all changes. The examples CI job is isolated and will be removed with the directory on rollback.

review_comments: Miguel Santos: Nice work — the devcontainer makes local testing frictionless. Left a comment about exposing only one port in docker-compose to avoid collisions.
Aisha Kapoor (author): Thanks — fixed compose ports and added a note in the README about common port ranges.
Priya Menon: Could we add a short section showing how to toggle the shim to call a real Redwood hosted endpoint? Requesting a small example config (done in docs/snippets/local-authoring-guides.md).

Jordan Lee: Unit tests look good. One flake in CI on macOS runner during `authorctl index` — I reran and it passed. Consider reducing default annoy trees for low-memory dev machines (updated CLI default to 4).

release_notes: Add local-first RAG Authoring Sandbox: reproducible devcontainer, authoring CLI, offline index builder (annoy fallback), validate-playground UI, and docs quickstart for local prompt/retrieval iteration.
